name: Prepare the annual report and audited financial statements (one annual report)
summary: Once a year the fund must give its annual report, with consolidated financial statements audited by the external auditor, to the federal and provincial finance ministers within 60 days of its March 31 year end and make it public. Fund accounting drafts the statements and notes from the approved year-end net asset value, Performance, Risk, Total Rewards and the Board secretariat write their sections, and Communications writes the narrative and produces the English and French editions. The draft passes a tie-out, director, auditor, controller, legal, CFRO and CEO review before the Audit Committee recommends it and the Board approves it. The work is squeezed into the six weeks after year end, so late valuations, auditor comments and changes that must be pushed through tie-out and translation again set the pace.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national pension fund investment manager with about 2,000 employees, one C$539 billion fund, IFRS statements and a Crown corporation reporting regime.
baseline.notes: Modelled on the model fund fiscal 2020 to 2022, when the Board approved the statements 42 to 45 days after year end and results were released about 50 days after year end. The case starts at the project kickoff in mid January and ends when the report is delivered to the ministers and published.

trigger: The fund accounting director opens the annual report project in mid January, about eleven weeks before the March 31 year end; the year-end performance report, the audit report and the compensation decisions feed it as they arrive.
end_state: The Board-approved annual report with audited statements is delivered to the federal and provincial finance ministers within 60 days of year end and published in English and French.

volume.seasonality: One report a year; the work runs from January to late May and peaks in the six weeks after the March 31 year end.

evidence.note: One annual report each financial year under s. 51.

steps.name: Kick off the annual report project
steps.description: In mid January the fund accounting director and the communications lead open the project: they confirm the publication date working back from the 60-day statutory deadline, the page plan, section owners (Finance, Performance, Risk, Total Rewards, Board secretariat, Communications) and the drafting and review timetable, and circulate it to contributors.

error.defect_description: Timetable leaves too little time between Board approval and delivery, or a section has no owner.

evidence.note: ICAEW recommends an executive sponsor, project manager, section owners and a timetable; working back from the s. 51 deadline. Mid January start is an estimate.

steps.name: Agree the year-end timetable and key judgments with the auditor
steps.description: The director meets the external auditor's engagement team to fix dates for draft statements, fieldwork on valuations, Audit Committee and Board meetings and opinion signing, and to agree the treatment of new standards and significant judgments such as Level 3 fair values before year end.

error.defect_description: An accounting judgment is left open and resurfaces late in fieldwork.

evidence.note: ICAEW: resolve major estimates and judgments with auditors at planning; fair value is management's most critical estimate (F2022 report).

steps.name: Draft the narrative sections
steps.description: Communications specialists interview the Chair, CEO and department heads, then write the chair's report, president's message, strategy, people and investment highlight pages against the page plan, using last year's text and approved messages. Drafts go to owners for comment in two or three rounds.

error.defect_description: Narrative figures or claims that later disagree with the final statements or performance numbers.

evidence.note: ICAEW: draft narrative before financials are ready. Report sections from the F2022 table of contents. Hours are an estimate for roughly 80 pages of front material.

steps.name: Roll forward statement and note shells and update policies
steps.description: A senior associate copies last year's statements and notes into this year's working file, updates note structures for new or amended IFRS requirements and changes in holdings, and drafts accounting policy memos for new transaction types so that numbers can be dropped in after year end.

error.defect_description: A new disclosure requirement or note change is missed in the shell.

evidence.note: F2022 report describes monitoring of IASB changes (IBOR Phase 2 amendments in F2022); posting describes annual external reporting schedules. Hours estimated.

steps.name: Fiscal year ends and the year-end ledger cut-off runs
steps.description: The fiscal year ends on March 31 and the investment book of record runs the year-end cut-off. The annual report project waits on the calendar until then; narrative drafting continues in the background.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Fiscal year ends March 31 (F2022 report). Wait length follows from the mid January start.

steps.name: Receive the approved year-end NAV and draft the statements
steps.description: When the March close and year-end private valuations are approved, the senior associate pulls the final trial balance from the book of record and the private investments system, maps accounts to statement lines, fills the balance sheet, net income, changes in net assets and cash flow statements for the base and additional plan accounts, and casts them.

error.defect_description: Account mapped to the wrong statement line, or a classification or casting error.

evidence.note: Statements required by s. 39(4); annual external reporting schedules in the posting. The 5 to 13 day wait for the approved year-end close is an estimate consistent with Board approval 42 to 45 days after year end (F2020 to F2022 reports); drafting starts on preliminary numbers. Hours estimated.

steps.name: Collect note inputs from contributor teams
steps.description: An associate sends requests and chases Valuations for fair value hierarchy and Level 3 tables, Risk for market, credit and liquidity risk figures, Treasury for debt and collateral, Tax, and Legal for commitments, guarantees and subsidiaries, and logs what has arrived against the note checklist.

error.defect_description: A contributor schedule arrives on an old basis or is incomplete.

evidence.note: Note topics follow the F2022 report (fair value hierarchy, risk, commitments, subsidiaries); the request-and-chase pattern and hours are estimates.

steps.name: Draft the notes to the statements
steps.description: The senior associate writes the notes: accounting policies, fair value hierarchy and Level 3 movements and sensitivities, derivatives, risk management, debt, commitments and guarantees, related parties and subsidiaries. Each note table is built from the contributor schedules and checked against the ledger.

error.defect_description: Note table that does not agree with the statements or with the contributor schedule.

evidence.note: Notes from page 95 of the F2022 report; fair value is the most critical estimate. Hours estimated.

steps.name: Tie out statements and notes
steps.description: Associates tick and tie every figure in the statements and notes to the trial balance, contributor schedules and between notes, recalculate totals and percentages, and log each difference for the preparer to fix.

error.defect_description: A difference is ticked as agreed but is not.

control.basis: Disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting evaluated under the CEO/CFRO certification (COSO 2013)

evidence.note: DFIN describes tie-out steps and common errors; CEO/CFRO certification covers disclosure controls. Hours estimated for a report of about 150 pages.

steps.name: Director reviews statements and notes
steps.description: The fund accounting director reads the full statements and notes against the tie-out file and the prior year, challenges unusual movements and disclosures, and either signs the review checklist or sends notes back for correction.

error.defect_description: A judgmental disclosure is accepted that the auditor later challenges.

control.basis: Management review control within internal control over financial reporting, externally audited from fiscal 2022

evidence.note: Management review controls are part of the ICFR assessed by management and audited by Deloitte from F2022. Rework share estimated.

steps.name: Correct note tables and re-tie changed figures
steps.description: The senior associate works through the director's review comments, corrects the affected note tables or wording, re-ties only the changed figures to the schedules and ledger, and returns the marked pages for re-review.

error.defect_description: A correction introduces a new mismatch.

evidence.note: Correction effort after a review is an estimate.

steps.name: Write the performance sections of the MD&A
steps.description: The performance director takes the final annual and five-year returns and dollar value-added for the fund, departments and programs, writes the fund performance and department performance pages and key performance indicator tables, and agrees every figure to the signed-off performance report.

error.defect_description: A return or value-added figure in the text does not match the performance report.

evidence.note: MD&A contains Key Performance Indicators, Fund Composition and Performance, Investment Department Performance (F2022 contents). Hours estimated.

steps.name: Draft the financial and risk sections of the MD&A
steps.description: The fund accounting director assembles the MD&A sections on fund composition, costs, leverage, risk and financial policies and controls, using the reviewed statements, Risk's limit and exposure figures and the cost analysis, and writes the commentary on the year.

error.defect_description: Commentary that conflicts with a note disclosure or a performance figure.

evidence.note: MD&A sections from the F2022 contents (Managing Risks, Managing Costs, Financial Policies and Controls). Hours estimated.

steps.name: Draft the compensation discussion and analysis
steps.description: Total rewards specialists write the HRCC letter draft, incentive plan description and named executive compensation tables once the HRCC has approved incentive awards based on the five-year results, and agree pay figures to payroll and the award calculations.

error.defect_description: A pay table figure that does not match the award calculation.

evidence.note: Compensation Discussion and Analysis with HRCC letter and fiscal 2022 disclosures (F2022 contents); HRCC evaluates at year end. Drafting by specialists and hours are estimates.

steps.name: Draft the governance section
steps.description: The associate corporate secretary updates the governance practices section, committee mandates, Board attendance table and director biographies from the Board records, and confirms each director's details.

error.defect_description: Attendance or biography detail out of date.

evidence.note: Governance Practices section and Board attendance chart in the F2022 report. Hours estimated.

steps.name: Auditor reviews the draft statements, notes and MD&A
steps.description: The external auditor's team reads the draft statements and notes against its audit work, completes its disclosure checklist, reads the MD&A for consistency with the statements and returns a list of comments.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: the fund's governing act s. 40: annual auditor's report on the financial statements and the record of investments

evidence.note: Auditor's report required by s. 40; Deloitte audit described in the F2022 report. Review turnaround is an estimate.

steps.name: Clear auditor comments and update the drafts
steps.description: The senior associate works through the comment list, agrees wording changes or provides support, updates the statements, notes and MD&A, re-ties changed figures and sends a marked version back to the auditor.

error.defect_description: A change made for one comment breaks a cross-reference elsewhere.

evidence.note: Comment cycles are common practice; a second auditor review in one case in four is an estimate.

steps.name: Controller reviews the full report for consistency
steps.description: The Managing Director, Finance reads the whole draft report, front narrative included, checks key figures against the statements and performance report, looks for messages that disagree between sections and sends sections back to their owners when needed.

error.defect_description: An inconsistency between narrative and statements is missed.

control.basis: Disclosure controls and procedures evaluated under the CEO/CFRO certification

next.condition: sections sent back to owners for changes

evidence.note: ICAEW recommends a full review for consistency and balanced messaging; disclosure controls described in F2022. Rework share estimated.

steps.name: Legal review of the report
steps.description: The General Counsel's office reads the report for legal risk: forward-looking statements wording, governance and compensation disclosures, litigation and guarantee notes and statements about the mandate, and marks required changes.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Internal practice of legal review of public disclosures

evidence.note: The report carries a forward-looking statements disclaimer (F2022 report); legal review as a separate step is common practice and an estimate.

steps.name: CFRO reviews and signs off statements and MD&A
steps.description: The Chief Financial and Risk Officer reviews the statements, MD&A and certification support, discusses open judgments with the controller and auditor, and signs the management representation letter and his part of the management responsibility statement.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: CEO/CFRO certification of internal control over financial reporting and disclosure controls (voluntary, not required by law)

evidence.note: F2022 report: CEO and CFRO certification performed voluntarily; CFRO signs Management's Responsibility for Financial Reporting.

steps.name: CEO reviews the report and signs management's responsibility
steps.description: The President and CEO reviews the president's message and the overall report, asks for final wording changes and signs Management's Responsibility for Financial Reporting and the certification together with the CFRO.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: CEO/CFRO certification and management responsibility statement

evidence.note: Management's Responsibility for Financial Reporting is signed by the CEO and CFRO (F2022, dated May 12, 2022).

steps.name: Prepare the Audit Committee and Board package
steps.description: A board secretariat specialist assembles the draft annual report, statements, auditor's report draft, certification memo and cover papers, checks that versions match, and posts the package to the board portal ahead of the meetings.

error.defect_description: An outdated version posted to the portal.

evidence.note: Audit Committee and Board review the statements before approval (F2022). Package preparation detail estimated.

steps.name: Audit Committee reviews and recommends the statements
steps.description: At its scheduled May meeting the Audit Committee meets management and the auditor, reviews the statements, MD&A and auditor's findings, meets the auditor without management and recommends the statements and MD&A to the Board.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: the fund's governing act s. 31(c) and (d): audit committee reviews the annual statements and meets the auditor before Board approval

evidence.note: Duty set by s. 31; F2022 report describes the committee recommending statements and MD&A and meeting auditors separately. Five Audit Committee meetings in F2022.

steps.name: Board approves the statements and annual report
steps.description: The Board of Directors approves the consolidated statements and the annual report; a director signs to evidence approval and the Audit Committee chair signs the Investment Certificate on behalf of the Board.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: the fund's governing act s. 39(7): board approves the annual statements, evidenced by a director's signature; Investment Certificate required by the Act

evidence.note: Board approval dates May 15, 2020, May 13, 2021 and May 12, 2022 (42 to 45 days after year end); certificate signed by the Audit Committee chair.

steps.name: Auditor signs and releases the audit opinion
steps.description: After its subsequent events procedures the external auditor signs the independent auditor's report on the statements and, from fiscal 2022, on internal control over financial reporting, and releases it for inclusion in the report.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: the fund's governing act s. 40 and s. 51(3)(b): auditor's report included in the annual report

evidence.note: Auditor's reports dated May 18, 2020 (3 days after Board approval), May 13, 2021 (same day) and May 16, 2022 (4 days after).

steps.name: Typeset, translate and proof the final report
steps.description: Communications specialists send final approved text to the design agency for typesetting and to translators for the French edition, check designer proofs page by page, and push late changes through both languages. Earlier sections were translated in batches during drafting.

error.defect_description: Typesetting or translation error in a figure, table or cross-reference.

evidence.note: About 73,000 words in the F2022 report text; translation runs at about 2,500 words a translator-day so it must be staged; French edition offered (F2022 report); ICAEW stresses proof checks. Hours estimated.

steps.name: Tie out the typeset report to the approved statements
steps.description: Associates compare every figure in the typeset English and French proofs with the approved statements and tie-out file, check page references and cross-references, and send a correction list to Communications.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Disclosure controls: published report must agree with Board-approved statements

evidence.note: Tie-out and printer proof checks; correction rate estimated.

steps.name: Push proof corrections through design and translation
steps.description: A communications specialist sends the correction list to the designer and translators, checks the corrected English and French pages, and has the associate re-check the changed figures before the files are released.

error.defect_description: A correction is applied in one language only.

evidence.note: ICAEW on proof checks; second-linguist review adds time. Effort and repeat rate estimated.

steps.name: Deliver the report to the ministers and publish it
steps.description: The associate corporate secretary sends the annual report to the federal Minister of Finance and the provincial finance ministers within the 60-day limit, confirms receipt, and Communications posts it on the website for the public and the results release.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: the fund's governing act s. 51(1): report to the Minister and provincial ministers within 60 days after year end and made public

evidence.note: 60-day limit and publication from s. 51(1); results released May 19, 2022.

exceptions.name: Auditor re-reviews significant changes
exceptions.description: Changes made to clear auditor comments, often on Level 3 fair value tables or new disclosures, are large enough that the auditor reviews the marked draft again.

exceptions.name: Director sends notes back
exceptions.description: The director's review finds note tables or disclosures that need rework before the MD&A can be finished.

exceptions.name: Controller sends sections back
exceptions.description: The controller finds messages or figures that disagree between the narrative, MD&A and statements and returns sections to their owners.

exceptions.name: Late changes after Board review
exceptions.description: The CFRO or the Audit Committee asks for wording or disclosure changes that must be cleared with the auditor and re-tied.

exceptions.name: Proof corrections
exceptions.description: The tie-out of the typeset proofs finds figures, page references or French text that differ from the approved version and the designer must correct them.

exceptions.name: Special examination year
exceptions.description: In the year a statutory special examination is completed (at least every six years, most recently February 2022) its results are reported, adding content and Audit Committee time without changing the path.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from project kickoff in mid January to delivery and publication
benchmarks.population: Canadian national pension fund with a March 31 year end, fiscal 2020 to 2022

evidence.note: Built from about 75 days of pre-year-end planning (estimate) plus the observed 49 to 50 days from year end to results release and the 60-day statutory limit; the elapsed time after year end is tier A, the kickoff date is an estimate.
Auditor's reports dated May 18, 2020, May 13, 2021 and May 16, 2022.

benchmarks.unit: days after year end to deliver the annual report to ministers
average days from year end to audit opinion by sextile
benchmarks.population: US public companies in the Blankley et al. study summarised by Audit Analytics

evidence.note: Fastest, middle and slowest sextile averages; a comparison point showing the fund reports faster than many listed companies.
Starting benchmark; lower for technical and marketing text.

pain_points.description: Statements and notes cannot be finished until the year-end close and private valuations are approved, which compresses drafting, review and audit into about four weeks.

evidence.note: Board approval 42 to 45 days after year end leaves roughly four weeks after the close; the squeeze is an inference.

pain_points.description: Every late change has to be re-tied, re-reviewed by the auditor and pushed through typesetting and French translation again.

evidence.note: ICAEW names late changes and proof checks; translation and second-linguist review add days.

pain_points.description: Figures are typed by hand from spreadsheets into Word and design files, so the same number appears in many places and tie-outs are long and repeated.

evidence.note: DFIN describes manual tie-out as time-intensive with transposition errors.

pain_points.description: Narrative written before year end can drift from final numbers and messages, and the inconsistency is found only at the controller's full read.

evidence.note: ICAEW recommends early narrative drafting and a later full consistency review.

pain_points.description: Many senior reviewers in sequence (director, auditor, controller, legal, CFRO, CEO, Audit Committee, Board) each wait on calendars in the same weeks.

evidence.note: Reviewer sequence from the report's signatures and governance; calendar contention is an estimate.

assumptions: The case starts at a project kickoff in mid January (tier C) so the elapsed time includes about 75 days before year end; the 49 to 56 days after year end are anchored on observed approval, opinion and release dates.

The three process map triggers (performance report, audit report, compensation decision) are all needed and none alone starts the case; the shares are nominal. The year-end net asset value and valuations are listed as standing inputs although the process map does not list them for this process.

Touch minutes are total person-minutes for a team; the simulator adds them to elapsed time as if one person worked serially, so waits after year end are set short to keep the post-year-end span near the observed 49 to 56 days.
The external audit fieldwork itself belongs to the separate external audit support process; this workflow keeps only the auditor's review of drafts and its opinion as outside waits.
Board, Audit Committee and auditor steps are outside parties (role external) because the organisation file models them as external parties.

Rewards specialists, the board secretariat specialist, associates in fund accounting and the CEO are added from the organisation file although the process map does not list them; the head of total rewards' review is folded into the specialists' drafting step, and the Managing Director, Corporate Communications' theme and final file approvals are folded into the kickoff and the production steps, so neither process map role has its own step.
FTE figures are annual hours on this process divided by about 1,560 working hours; staffing on this one annual case is small compared with the headcount of each role.
Loaded hourly costs come from the organisation file, which scales compensation to personnel expenses with an overhead factor of 1.25.
